analysis.title: Monday Kick-off
key_insights: Markets open the week steadier after a sharp selloff. AI and momentum names rebounded Friday, and the report says technical factors and stretched positioning drove both the decline and the bounce.

Thursday was one of the toughest US equity sessions in recent months. After the post-midterm Democratic sweep, the Nasdaq fell into correction territory, the Mag 7 lost roughly USD 1T, and semiconductors had their worst day since March 2020 on AI-investment constraint and softer growth concerns.
Friday's October jobs report was described as a blowout. The 2-year US Treasury yield rose 14 basis points to 4.25% and traders now price a 70% probability of a December Fed rate hike.
Oil finished the week lower as markets leaned toward diplomatic de-escalation in the Middle East, despite Trump consulting advisers on possible renewed Iran strikes.
The key question for the week is whether markets stabilise after the positioning reset. Politics and macro data, especially Tuesday's CPI, are expected to set the tone.

The Exposure Optimisation Model puts global equity exposure at 70%, down from 71%. Europe rose to 90% from 69%, Asia fell to 46% from 60%, and US exposure is described as stable at 70% (the text says 73 to 70%, which is internally inconsistent).

Technical View: the two pillars of this year's rally, semiconductors and the Mag-7, are under pressure from earnings disappointment and monetisation concerns. The midterm sweep triggered risk-off in AI infrastructure, and volatility could stay elevated until key supports hold.

Healthcare has regained relative strength in the US and Europe as the tech selloff prompted a rotation to defensives. Elevated US valuations and moderating earnings upgrades are cautions, while European valuations are below their 10-year average.

European banks held technical support after French credit concerns pushed them to stretched levels. Friday's price action points to a possible tactical rebound, with a resilient macro backdrop and solid Q3 earnings.

Quality factor (QUAL) is near record highs but dispersion within it is unusually high. Momentum and High Beta lost leadership before the midterms, and the desk sees selectivity in AI rather than abandonment of growth. It screens for Quality laggards with intact fundamentals.

tension_points.bull_case: AI demand and earnings expectations remain strong for the time being, which suggests greater selectivity rather than an outright abandonment of growth.
tension_points.bear_case: The midterm sweep triggered risk-off in AI infrastructure, semis had their worst day since March 2020, and the Mag-7 and semis are under pressure on earnings disappointment and monetisation concerns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure of key support levels on the semiconductor and US tech charts would extend the pressure. The report gives no specific levels.
